attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Which sprite name should be used as the argument in the sprite parameter of the createProjectileFromSprite code for the playerProjectile ?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which sprite should send the projectile in the createProjectileFromSprite code?


Solution: 

The argument in the sprite parameter of the createProjectileFromSprite code should be changed from enemySprite to playerSprite
steps.instructions:
When the A button is pressed, a projectile is sent from the wrong sprite!


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the A button is pressed, the Player sprite sends a projectile towards the Enemy sprite.

subgroups.title: Debugging Sprite Kinds and Projectiles
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: sprite parameter in createProjectileFromSprite code changed to playerSprite.
validationItems.failureText: Check the sprite parameter in the createProjectileFromSprite code.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Where should the enemyProjectile.setKind code be moved so that the program can access the sprite code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Where is the enemyProjectile created in the code? Where should its sprite kind be set?


Solution: 

The code on Line 220 should be cut and pasted in between the createProjectileFromSprite code and the setPosition code on Line 217.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 220: the program cannot find the name ‘enemyProjectile’. 

Fix the bugs in the code so that whenever an enemyProjectile is created, its sprite kind is changed to EnemyProjectile.

validationItems.text: Code on Line 220 is cut and pasted in between the createProjectileFromSprite code and the setPosition code.
validationItems.failureText: Check where the enemyProjectile’s sprite kind is set in the code.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ What sprite kind should the kind parameter be set to so the onOverlap code will run when a PlayerProjectile overlaps the Enemy sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What sprite kind should the kind parameter be changed to in the onOverlap event?


Solution: 

The kind parameter in the PlayerProjectile/Enemy onOverlap event should be changed to SpriteKind.PlayerProjectile.
steps.instructions:
When a PlayerProjectile overlaps the Enemy sprite, nothing happens!


Fix the bugs in the code so that when a PlayerProjectile overlaps the Enemy sprite, the PlayerProjectile is destroyed and the Player sprite’s score increases by 1.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓ What parameter should be used in place of the sprite name so that the Player sprite is destroyed when it is overlapped by an EnemyProjectile?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which handler function parameter refers to the sprite kind named in the kind parameter of the onOverlap event?


Solution: 

otherSprite should be replaced with sprite in the destroy code in the EnemyProjectile/Player overlap event.
steps.instructions:
When an EnemyProjectile overlaps the Player sprite, the Player sprite is destroyed.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the EnemyProjectile is destroyed on overlap with the Player sprite.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about sprite kinds and sprite overlap events. In the JavaScript editor, you can use a namespace to create new sprite kinds. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: One of a Kind
badges.description: Use sprite kinds and events to control what happens to sprites in a project in JavaScript.

badges.title: A Meeting of the Kinds
badges.description: Use an overlap event that runs based on the sprites’ kinds.

badges.title: Nice Knowing Ya
badges.description: Write code that destroys a sprite.

badges.title: Life of the Party
badges.description: Set the value of the Player’s life.

badges.title: From One Sprite to Another
badges.description: Create a projectile that starts from the position of an existing sprite.

badges.title: Metamorphosis
badges.description: Change the sprite kind of an existing sprite.

badges.title: Kind of You to Join
badges.description: Create a new sprite kind in JavaScript.

badges.title: New Kind on the Block
badges.description: Write code that runs when a sprite with a specific sprite kind is created.

badges.title: Out of Chances
badges.description: Write code that runs when the Player’s life reaches zero.

badges.title: Spice Up Your Life
badges.description: Set the image used to represent the Player’s life.
